h: "For You" on Atzeres: The Eating That Is Like an Offering

p: It is the day on which the Torah was given.
We have already spoken about this
from the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
it is written "an assembly to Hashem your God" (Devarim 16:8),
and it is written "an assembly shall it be for you" (Bamidbar 29:35);
half of it for Hashem and half of it for you,
or all of it for Hashem, etc.,
Now in truth the two pesukim were stated
Regarding the seventh day of Pesach
it says "shall it be for you."
they learned through a gezeirah shavah
to apply what is said of this one to that one.
the mitzvah lies specifically upon the outer garment,
from the pleasures of this world in actual fact,
by eating the bread of affliction.
which is the season of our rejoicing,
that is, upon the outer garment
there should be the aspect of "for you."
And this is the purpose of the derivation
to apply what is said of this one to that one:
meaning that the body too should enjoy
and feel vitality from the kedushah
as it does from the matters of this world;
and on the festival of Shemini Atzeres
the "for you" should also be "for Hashem,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם כׇּל הֲנָאוֹת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
meaning that all the pleasures of this world as well
should be solely for Hashem alone.
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה:
that the "for you" should also be "for Hashem";
It is the day on which the Torah was given.
For through the power of the Torah
upon all the creations in this world,
is only to do the will of their Maker,
as it says in the Gemara (Chullin 7a)
"I am going to do the will of my Maker,"
that is, without any free choice on its part.
And just as it was in this aspect
״אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט),
and the delights of this world
מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, טז).
of every tree of the garden you may surely eat" (Bereishis 2:16).
And with this we will also understand
that it was a fast over a dream,
and therefore even on Shabbos and Yom Tov,
it is permitted to sit in fasting,
regarding which the term "feasting" is used;
eating itself is reckoned as a fast,
"as though he fasted on the ninth," etc.;
the time when the Torah was given,
of the intent of a fast,
that "the diminishing of my fat and blood should be
as though I had offered a korban."
And this is found stated explicitly
regarding the eating of talmidei chachamim:
one who brings a gift to a talmid chacham
is as though he offered bikkurim (Kesubos 105b);
and one who wishes to pour a libation of wine
שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן (יוֹמָא עא, א);
״אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים עוֹבֵר עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד״ (מְלָכִים ב ד, ט),
"a man of God passes by us continually" (Melachim II 4:9),
whoever hosts a talmid chacham in his home
is as though he offered the daily korbanos.
even a fast over a dream is forbidden,

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 68b — "One verse says, 'an assembly to Hashem your God,' and one verse says, 'an assembly shall it be to you.' Rabbi Eliezer holds: either all of it for Hashem or all of it for you; Rabbi Yehoshua holds: divide it — half for Hashem and half for you." The Gemara continues: all agree that on Atzeres (Shavuos) "for you" is also needed. Rashi: that one rejoices on it with food and drink.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushas Levi, Shavuos — “In Pesachim 68b we say: ‘All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require “for you.”’ That is, on Pesach a person rejoices because his body rejoices at going out from slavery, which is a bodily good. But on Shavuos the joy is over the giving of the Torah, and it would be hard for the body to rejoice, since Matan Torah is only a spiritual good. Therefore they said that on Atzeres we also require ‘for you’: that the body should rejoice, believing that the Torah is the life of the World to Come and of this world.” Connection: The same Gemara read, as Rav Tzadok reads it, as the inclusion of the body's enjoyment in the holiness of Matan Torah.

paragraphs.text: Commentary: Rashi on Devarim 16:8 — “‘An assembly (atzeres) to Hashem your God’: hold yourself back from work. Another explanation: a gathering of food and drink, from the expression ‘let us detain (na'tzerah) you’ (Shoftim 13:15).” Connection: Rashi's second reading, that “atzeres” is a gathering for eating and drinking, bears on the maamar's question of how the festival can be “for you.”

paragraphs.text: Chullin 7a — "He said to the river Ginai: Ginai, divide your waters for me and I will pass through you. It said: You go to do the will of your Maker, and I go to do the will of my Maker; you may or may not accomplish it, while I certainly accomplish it. He said: If you do not divide, I decree that water never pass through you again. It divided for him."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 68b — "Mar the son of Ravina would sit in fasting the whole year except on Atzeres, Purim and Erev Yom Kippur: Atzeres — the day the Torah was given; Purim — 'days of feasting and joy' is written; Erev Yom Kippur — as Chiya bar Rav of Difti taught: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth is regarded as though he fasted on the ninth and the tenth."

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Berachos 49b (s.v. i ba'i achil) — As for what is said (Pesachim 68b), that Mar the son of Ravina would sit in fast all year, implying that he fasted even on Yom Tov: the Ri explains that this refers to a fast over a dream, but other fasts are forbidden [on Yom Tov].

paragraphs.text: Yoma 81b — "Chiya bar Rav of Difti taught: 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth' (Vayikra 23:32) — do they fast on the ninth? Do they not fast on the tenth? Rather, to tell you: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, Scripture regards him as though he fasted on the ninth and the tenth." Rashi: prepare yourself on the ninth so that you will be able to fast on the tenth.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — "When Rav Sheshes sat in a fast, after praying he would say: Master of the worlds, it is revealed before You that when the Beis HaMikdash stood, a person who sinned brought an offering, and only its fat and blood were offered, and he was atoned. Now I have sat in a fast and my fat and blood have diminished; may it be Your will that my diminished fat and blood be as though I had offered them before You on the altar."

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 105b — "'And a man came from Baal Shalishah and brought the man of God bread of the first fruits' (II Melachim 4:42) — did Elisha eat first fruits? Rather, to tell you: whoever brings a gift to a Torah scholar is as though he offered first fruits."

paragraphs.text: Yoma 71a — "'To you, O men (ishim), I call' (Mishlei 8:4). Rabbi Berechyah said: These are Torah scholars, who are like women yet do mighty deeds like men. And Rabbi Berechyah said: One who wishes to pour a libation of wine upon the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine." Rashi: ishim recalls the fire-offerings (ishim).

paragraphs.text: Berachos 10b — "'[A holy man of God] passes by us continually' (II Melachim 4:9): Rabbi Yosi bar Chanina said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov: Whoever hosts a Torah scholar in his home and lets him benefit from his possessions, Scripture regards him as though he offered the daily offerings."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 3 — “There is a meal from the level of the sage, as it says in the holy Zohar (II 61b): ‘Higher than all is the nourishment of the companions… the nourishment of spirit and soul’… This is eating in holiness far more than a mitzvah… and it is called ‘the table that is before Hashem,’ which is like an actual offering. As we find (Berachos 10b): whoever hosts a Torah scholar in his home is as if he offered the daily offerings; and it says (Yoma 71a): whoever wishes to pour a libation of wine on the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine.” Connection: The same Gemaras on eating that is like an offering, the theme Rav Tzadok draws from “for you” on Atzeres.
